text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ADEVARUL
- The price of natural gas is expected to rise to 340 lei per cubic metre within the next two weeks.
- Sailors in the Black Sea port of Constanta staged a rally on Tuesday demanding more rights and to protest against shipowners who failed to pay their wages.
- The support given by the World Bank to Romania will boost foriegn investors' confidence in the Balkan country, Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara is quoted as saying.
- Workers at the Semanatoarea SA farming equipment maker threatened to strike on Thursday.

- Prosecutors banned local businessman George Paunescu from leaving Bucharest over the next 30 days. The authorities are investigating alleged irregularities related to the purchase of shares worth $10 million in the Credit Bank commercial bank.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The central bank decided to raise to 50 billion lei, from a previous 25 billion, the capital needed to open a bank.
- Train fares and freight tariffs have become prohibitive for many Romanians, the paper says.
- The Sidex SA steel mill in Galati exports some 60 percent of its output.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- A Hungarian company is interested in buying the troubled private Dacia Felix bank, the paper says.
- The State Ownership Fund plans to appoint a new management at the state-airline Tarom SA.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The State Ownership Fund plans to sell a controlling 51 percent interest through direct negotiations in five companies, including a steel mill and a shipyard on the Danube River.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The president of the Bucharest military court resigned saying the Justice Ministry repeatedly ignored his decisions.

- Adrian Nastase, first vice-president of the Social Democratic Party of Romania (PDSR), said recent statements by PDSR senator Ioan Solcanu on party activities served the interests of those trying to undermine the PDSR.
- Parliament's Chamber of Deputies legal commission is to discuss today a draft law on keeping state secrets.
- Deputies rejected a PDSR motion against road taxes saying it was "a premature electoral drill".

- Parties in the government coalition discussed amendments to the land law on Tuesday. The National Peasant Party (PNTCD), the National Liberal Party (PNL) and the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) are for giving back former owners an area of 50 hectares.
The Democratic Party (PD) said an area of 10 hectares would be enough.
- A commemorative Freddie Mercury photography show in the western city of Timisoara yielded 3.3 million lei from ticket sales. The money goes to HIV-infected children.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Democratic Convention intends to annul the existing law on house restitution. The new draft provides for the restitution "in integrum" to former owners.
ADEVARUL
- The Supreme Defence Council meets on Wednesday to discuss the appointment of a successor to Romanian Intelligence Service boss Virgil Magureanu, who resigned.
- A council set up four months ago to fight organised crime met for the first time saying reports drafted so far would be collated to assess "losses due to the underground economy".
Sources at the Cotroceni palace said overall losses might amount to 870 billion lei.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Adrian Nastase said there would be no contest in the election of PDSR's president, with senator and former Romanian President Ion Iliescu as the sole candidate. ($=7,090 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
